S1.why: The vocabulary's own label-colon-number shape (Cutlingov: %lld) keeps the number free of case endings; 13 characters with 5, one over the budget, chosen over the colloquial Zastonj so the word matches S28 and M3.

S2.why: An invitation in the vi imperative the vocabulary uses (Vklopite); no word about a limit.

S3.s: Porabili ste vseh %lld brezplačnih cutlingov. Ostanejo brezplačni in delujejo kot doslej.
S3.back: Used-up you-have all 5 free cutlings. They-stay free and work as till-now.
S3.why: Genitive plural after vseh %lld is right for 5; kot doslej says nothing changes for them without a promise-sounding phrase.

S4.why: Reads as a plain offer and avoids the 'lahko' (you can) construction; genitive plural is right for 5.

S5.why: 'od' takes the genitive plural whatever the first number is, so the sentence is right for 0 to 4 used; numbers keep English order, so no positional forms.

S6.why: 'do' plus genitive plural fits one line at 18 characters; 'Prostor za' would run to 26.

S7.s: Shranite lahko do %@ besedil in %lld slik.
S7.back: Save you-can up-to 5,000 texts and 500 images.
S7.why: besedilo and slike from the vocabulary, both genitive plural after do; placeholders in brief order.

S8.why: Slovenian lists with 'in' and no comma before it; names stay in the nominative.

S9.s: En nakup velja za vse naprave, prijavljene v vaš Apple račun.
S9.back: One purchase applies for all devices, signed-in into your Apple account.
S9.why: Uses the vocabulary's phrase 'prijavljeni v vaš Apple račun' and its 'Apple račun'.

S10.why: A verb with the person in it, vi form, 19 characters.

S11.why: One 'brez' governing three genitives is how a Slovenian writes it; registracija is the everyday word for signing up, and avoids a second 'račun' next to Apple račun.

S12.why: The wording Slovenian iOS apps use for the App Store restore action; button and link form is the bare imperative, like the vocabulary's Nadaljuj.

S13.why: The verbal noun for a running process, ending with the single ellipsis character.

S14.why: Bare imperative like Nadaljuj; 'once' stays in S10 directly above, because an adjective such as enkratnih would have to agree with whatever currency %@ brings.

S15.why: S14 without the price; Odkleni Cutling would be 15 characters against a 14 budget.

S16.why: The ordinary way to put something off in Slovenian; pozneje is the standard form over colloquial kasneje.

S17.why: The verb iOS uses on Slovenian close buttons.

S18.why: Short and warm, vi possessive; 'vse' covers the items and the room without listing them.

S19.s: Hvala za nakup. Podprli ste Cutling in človeka, ki ga sam razvija.
S19.back: Thanks for purchase. Supported you-have Cutling and person, who it alone develops.
S19.why: 'človeka' keeps the maker's gender open; 'sam' says one person makes it without the word 'edini'.

S20.s: Dobrodošli nazaj. Vaš nakup je obnovljen.
S20.back: Welcome back. Your purchase is restored.
S20.why: Obnovljen ties to the Obnovi nakupe link they just tapped; vi plural greeting.

S21.why: Same sentence as S5, spoken, so the eye and ear get one wording; 'od' plus genitive plural works for any used count.

S22.why: Slovenian has four number forms (1, 2, 3-4, 5+), so the count goes after a colon as in the vocabulary's Cutlingov: %lld; right for 1, 2, 5 and 21.

S23.s: Cutling je odklenjen. Prostora je za %@ cutlingov.
S23.back: Cutling is unlocked. Room is for 5,000 cutlings.
S23.why: Cutling as the app name, masculine; genitive plural is right after 5.000.

S24.why: The calm standard phrase; it names what happened and blames no one.

S25.s: Trgovina App Store trenutno ni dosegljiva. Poskusite znova malo pozneje.
S25.back: Store App Store currently not reachable. Try again a-little later.
S25.why: 'Trgovina App Store' gives the name a feminine noun to agree with instead of declining App Store.

S26.s: Trgovina App Store tega nakupa ni potrdila.
S26.back: Store App Store this purchase not confirmed.
S26.why: Same 'Trgovina App Store' frame as S25; states the fact, no blame.

S27.s: Apple račun v tej napravi nima prejšnjega nakupa Cutlinga.
S27.back: Apple account in this device has-not earlier purchase of-Cutling.
S27.why: Apple račun from the vocabulary; the genitive Cutlinga is how Slovenian writes an app name as the object of a purchase.

S28.s: Brezplačna različica hrani %lld cutlingov. Ko Cutling enkrat odklenete, shranite, kolikor želite.
S28.back: Free version holds 5 cutlings. When Cutling once you-unlock, you-save, as-much-as you-wish.
S28.why: Siri speaks in the app's vi form; genitive plural right for 5; 'enkrat' carries the one-time purchase.

S29.why: The vocabulary's own count line (Cutlingov: %lld) with its cap added, so a free copy's subtitle is the same line, not a new one; 17 characters.

M6.why: Device names declined in the locative (iPhonu, iPadu, Macu) as Slovenian writers do; 'in' list, no serial comma.

M7.s: Odklenjeno na iPhonu, iPadu in Macu s tem Apple računom.
M7.back: Unlocked on iPhone, iPad and Mac with this Apple account.
M7.why: Impersonal neuter 'Odklenjeno' suits a status line; Apple račun in the instrumental.
